clue.text: Chance of crop pest being dispersed

indicators.note: things dispersed are scattered about, so these letters are spread and regathered in a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer weighs the odds of a crop-eating pest spreading through the fields.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a likelihood of something happening, the same as a chance of it.

clue.text: Change the start of a country trip

indicators.note: changing the start means the opening letter of the following word is swapped for another

explanation.surface: Someone suggests altering the first leg of a journey around a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: FRANCE has its first letter changed to P to give PRANCE; the clue does not name the new letter, so the definition and crossings must supply it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip is to move with light, lively steps, which is what prancing describes.

clue.text: Widespread public disapproval of demand made by cricketers?

blocks.note: first meaning: a loud public protest
second meaning, read literally: the shout of the fielders appealing for a batsman to be given out

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the fielding side appeal to the umpire by shouting for the batsman to be ruled out, so the answer split in two is literally their cry.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a strong, widely voiced protest by the public against something.

clue.text: Did agent put up with behaviour by journalist?

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written upwards, so the word runs bottom to top

blocks.note: a rep is a sales agent
form as in good or bad form, conduct
ED is short for editor, the standard crossword journalist; by places it at the end

explanation.surface: A question whether a talent agent tolerated a reporter's conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'put up' turns the agent upwards; FORM here is conduct as in 'bad form'.
explanation.definitionFit: Performed means carried out or acted, a past-tense synonym of did.

clue.text: Do dull chores badly to show lack of interest

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters come out in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Doing household tasks sloppily is a way of signalling you couldn't care less.
explanation.definitionFit: To cold-shoulder someone is to ignore them deliberately, treating them with indifference.

clue.text: Victoria was famously not so pleasantly occupied

blocks.note: first meaning: Queen Victoria is supposed to have said 'We are not ...'

explanation.walkthrough: The first half relies on the famous line attributed to Queen Victoria, 'We are not amused'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone kept entertained and diverted is pleasantly occupied; the queen's quip denies that state.

clue.text: Good to swap hands used for grinding

indicators.note: the hands are left and right, and swapping them exchanges those two letters within the word

blocks.note: moral as an adjective means good, virtuous

explanation.surface: An instruction to change hands while doing something worthwhile.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R stand for left and right hands; in MORAL the R and L trade places to give MOLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A molar is a back tooth, one whose broad surface is used to grind food.

clue.text: Rear section of orchestra might not be seen to start immediately

indicators.note: a rear section is only the back part, so the front of the word is dropped and its tail kept
the start not being seen means the first letter goes missing

blocks.note: taken as written before its front is cut away
taken as written before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: Players at the back of the orchestra may not be noticed coming in on cue.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight, as in 'go straight there', means at once, without delay.

clue.text: Steps down as director before essential service contract initially expires

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for director
something that expires comes to an end

explanation.surface: A director resigns before the key service agreement runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply puts D ahead of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To descend is to go down, so the answer as a verb means steps down.

clue.text: A fellow's half-sister has everything, contrary to expectations

indicators.note: half of the word means only one of its two halves is kept and the other dropped

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
taken as written before it is halved

explanation.surface: A man's half-sister, it turns out, owns the lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The back half of SISTER is kept; the hyphen makes 'half-sister' look like a family relation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used for an outcome that happens despite what was expected, as in 'it rained after all'.

clue.text: '70s trousers are appearing in films regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is taken
appearing in means placed inside the other letters

explanation.surface: Bell-bottom trousers keep turning up in movies.
explanation.definitionFit: Flares are wide-bottomed trousers, a fashion strongly associated with the 1970s.

clue.text: Put sheet carelessly on vessel and capsize

indicators.note: doing something carelessly leaves things disordered, so these letters end up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Throwing a sheet down sloppily on a dinghy tips it over.
explanation.definitionFit: To capsize a vessel is to overturn it, which is the literal sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Goods travel on the back of a small vehicle

indicators.note: placed on the back of means coming after, so this part follows the other

blocks.note: a car is a small vehicle

explanation.surface: Freight is carried strapped behind a little van.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the freight carried by a ship or vehicle, the goods it transports.

clue.text: Keep an eye on American-backed reps I've employed

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the letters run in the opposite direction
employed suggests letters put to work in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A manager says to watch over the sales staff hired with US funding.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise is to oversee or watch over someone's work.

clue.text: Poor little devil with more than one cast off

blocks.note: an imp is a small devil
I is the Roman numeral for one
shed means cast off, as a snake its skin

explanation.surface: A wretched imp sheds several layers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than one' looks like a single phrase but splits: 'more than' and 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Impoverished means reduced to poverty, a fuller word for poor.

clue.text: Order in dialect is the same in every way

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A remark that a request made in local speech means exactly the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical things match in every respect, alike in all details.

clue.text: Give out drugs for heartless disease gripping writers

indicators.note: heartless means the central letters of the word are taken out
gripping means holding on to something placed inside

blocks.note: taken as written before its middle goes

explanation.surface: A pharmacist hands out medicine for an illness that has gripped some authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the three central letters here, not just one, leaving two letters at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharmacists dispense medicines, meaning they prepare and hand them out to patients.

clue.text: Authorised chemical company to separate waste parts of carcass

indicators.note: to separate something is to come between its parts, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a former British chemical giant
offal is the discarded innards of a slaughtered animal

explanation.surface: A licensed chemicals firm sorts the leftover bits of an animal carcass.
explanation.definitionFit: Something official has been approved by authority, so it is authorised.

clue.text: Betrayals come from unbeliever, it is said

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the words are judged by how they sound

blocks.note: an infidel is an unbeliever, followed by the words it is

explanation.surface: Acts of treachery are blamed on a heathen, so people claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Infidelities are acts of unfaithfulness, betrayals of a partner's trust.

clue.text: Am in a big muddle in Africa

indicators.note: a muddle is a mess, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A traveller confesses to being thoroughly confused somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'in Africa' stands for a country found there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gambia is a small West African country, a place located in Africa.

clue.text: Source of danger that surrounds soldiers

indicators.note: surrounds means wraps around another piece

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a regiment of the British Army

explanation.surface: A peril that closes in around troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is something likely to cause harm, a source of danger.

clue.text: Favour prig over depraved candidate, ultimately

indicators.note: over here means covering around, so the first word sits on either side of the second
ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: Choosing a prude ahead of a corrupt nominee for an election.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special advantage or favour granted to someone.

clue.text: Some laid Easter plans

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: Some people made arrangements for the Easter holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas can be schemes or intentions, the same as plans for doing something.

clue.text: Give lessons in corporate achievement

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the following words

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: Run training sessions on business success.
explanation.definitionFit: To teach is to instruct, which is what giving lessons means.

clue.text: Captured knight was in poor health

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight taken prisoner had been sickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail someone is informal for catching them, so nailed means captured.

clue.text: Catholic admitted to weakness in using violence

indicators.note: someone admitted to a place goes inside it

blocks.note: a foible is a minor weakness of character

explanation.surface: A churchgoer confesses to a failing for brute force.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcible describes an action done by physical force, such as forcible entry.

clue.text: Amazingly, Len is on time to sign up

indicators.note: something amazing defies expectation, so these letters turn out in a surprising order

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time; on places it after

explanation.surface: Remarkably, Len turns up punctually to join the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to enrol, especially in the armed forces, which is to sign up.

clue.text: Loyal supporter is beginning to accept crazy law

indicators.note: crazy means wild, so the letters are thrown into a new order
accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A devoted backer is starting to embrace an insane piece of legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is a dependable, committed member of a group, a loyal supporter.
